name: Ajay Gummalla
current_role: Co-founder & VP of Engineering, Bedrock Robotics (San Francisco)
profile: Former Waymo engineering leader who co-founded Bedrock Robotics in 2024 with Boris Sofman, Kevin Peterson and Tom Eliaz. Bedrock retrofits excavators and other heavy construction equipment with autonomy kits; it emerged from stealth in July 2025 with ~$80M and has since raised large later rounds (Hurun: $2B+ valuation).
interesting_fact: Bedrock emerged from stealth in July 2025 with about $80M in seed and Series A funding to automate construction equipment, founded by a group of ex-Waymo self-driving engineers.
notes: Low public profile; no personal socials found. Patent databases list a prolific RF/antenna inventor of the same name (Rayspan, Broadcom, Google patents) - likely him but not confirmed, so not used as deep-cut. Best route: Bedrock press email.

name: Nathan Wolfe
current_role: Co-founder, EVP & CTO (as of 2022 reporting), Aalyria Technologies
profile: Former Google engineer who developed the free-space laser communications technology that became Aalyria's Tightbeam product. Aalyria spun out of Alphabet in 2022 with Tightbeam (laser links) and Spacetime (network orchestration software from the Loon project), led at launch by CEO Chris Taylor; co-founder Brian Barritt became CEO in 2026.
interesting_fact: Aalyria's Tightbeam grew out of Google's 'Project Sonora' and Loon-era work on steerable laser beams; Wolfe said the tech was designed for 'backhauling these large Google-scale volumes of data'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Aalyria, Wolfe worked at Google developing the technology that became Tightbeam; Tightbeam itself grew out of Google's internal Project Sonora.
notes: NAME COLLISION: not the virologist Nathan Wolfe (Metabiota/Global Viral, Stanford), who dominates search results and has a 2026 Epstein-correspondence controversy - do not confuse. Aalyria's Wolfe has a very low profile; current title after the 2026 CEO change not confirmed.

name: Roeland Delrue
profile: Belgian SaaS go-to-market executive who co-founded developer-first security platform Aikido Security in 2022 with Willem Delbare, Felix Garriau and Madeline Lawrence. Previously spent ~7 years at Ghent sales-enablement firm Showpad (product manager, account executive, sales leadership) and about a year at Officient; started as a corporate banking analyst at KBC.
interesting_fact: Aikido bills itself as the fastest European cybersecurity company to reach unicorn status - founded in 2022, now 350+ employees protecting 150k+ teams.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech, Delrue began his career as a corporate banking analyst at KBC Bank & Verzekering, then spent six-plus years at Showpad moving between product management and sales roles.
notes: Low media profile; LinkedIn (linked from Aikido's own About page) is the most direct route. Some sources title him CRO & COO; Aikido's site currently says COO.
